story: Taylor Meier and Evan Westfall met at summer camp as middle schoolers in Upper Arlington, near Columbus, Ohio, and built Caamp around that friendship. The 2016 self-titled debut on Square Roots included the breakout Ohio, and By and By, on Mom + Pop in 2019, topped Billboard's Heatseekers chart. They played Pickathon that year. Lavender Days, on June 24, 2022, reached No. 83 on the Billboard 200, and Apple Tree Blues landed on Barack Obama's summer playlist. Copper Changes Color arrived in 2025, and in 2026 they played amphitheaters, a long way from summer camp.
artist_reel_line: Lavender Days came in 2022 and Copper Changes Color in 2025.

intro: A Mississippi hill country blues drummer and bandleader.
story: Cedric Burnside was born in Memphis in 1978 and raised in Benton and Marshall Counties, Mississippi, where he played alongside his grandfather, the hill country blues pioneer R.L. Burnside, at house parties and juke joints. He was named Blues Music Awards Drummer of the Year four years in a row before leading his own band. He played Pickathon in 2019, the year after Benton County Relic, recorded with Brian Jay of Pimps of Joytime and nominated for Best Traditional Blues Album at the 2019 Grammys. Burnside has said that before it he always collaborated with others, and that record was the first on his own terms.
artist_reel_line: Benton County Relic, his first record on his own terms, was a 2019 Grammy nominee.

story: Laura Veirs is a songwriter from Colorado Springs who has recorded since 1999 and is based in Portland. The Lookout, her tenth studio album, came out April 13, 2018 on her own Raven Marching Band label, and NPR called it a buffer to a chaotic world; in 2016 she made case/lang/veirs with Neko Case and k.d. lang. She played Pickathon in 2019. Found Light, on July 8, 2022, was her first album without the producer Tucker Martine since 2001. She co-produced it with Shahzad Ismaily and says it was the first time she asked herself what she wanted the music to sound like. Phone Orphans came in 2023, and in 2026 she recorded Temple Songs in her backyard studio.
artist_reel_line: Found Light, in 2022, was her first album without producer Tucker Martine since 2001.

story: Mountain Man began in 2010 when Molly Sarle, Alexandra Sauser-Monnig and Amelia Meath were students at Bennington College, and they first released Made the Harbor on Myspace. Magic Ship, their first album in eight years and first for Nonesuch, came out September 21, 2018 and reached No. 12 on Billboard Heatseekers, and NPR praised their almost supernatural harmonizing. They played Pickathon in 2019. Each of the three keeps a project of her own: Meath records as half of Sylvan Esso, and Sauser-Monnig released Dawnbreaker as Daughter of Swords on June 28, 2019.
artist_reel_line: Meath also records as half of Sylvan Esso; Sauser-Monnig released Dawnbreaker in 2019.
